newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes up with WTI, focus on Mexico.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes up with WTI, focus on Mexico.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose moderately late Tuesday, lifted by higher benchmark domestic crude, while local trade wondered who would buy revived Mexican crude exports.
The head of Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), Mexicos state oil firm, said Tuesday his company is looking to sell Mayan crude to West Coast refiners.

Pemex, burdened by overproduction, is looking to boost exports to the West Coast as that region's intake of Alaskan crude falls. Several refiners, including, Ultramar, Shell, and Mobil, said they had not bought the crude contracts.
But one refinery trader heard Shell may be the buyers.
Shell could not be reached for comment.
Outright prices for ANS crude rose 50 cents Tuesday to $18.98/19.18 a barrel, with the last deal done two weeks ago at $1.32 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
WTI spot prices 55 cents a barrel Tuesday on technical buying in the futures market.
BP, the crude's main producer, priced their barrels at $1.15 under WTI, buyers said.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
Traders reported no deals in Line 63 and heavy California grades.
